The key drag was the IT security product sales operation , where GM dived to 16.2% from 23.6% in 1Q25. The slight YoY c ore profit growth was supported by a 3% YoY revenue increase. The QoQ dive was due to seasonality —the first -quarter is normally a weak period for commercial project sales (which peak in the fourth-quarter). SIS marked an SG&A/sales ratio of 4.4%, up 50bps QoQ. Including FX gains of Bt70m, the 1Q26 bottom-line was Bt258m, up 28% YoY but down 2% QoQ. Result highlights Revenue totaled Bt7.6bn in 1Q26 , up 3% YoY. Growth was driven by Value Products (24% of revenue ), up by 14% YoY, led by demand for cybersecurity solutions, Audio -Visual, and Software as a Service (SaaS). Volume Product sales (76% of revenue) were flat YoY, due to weak consumer purchasing power /willingness to spend . 1Q26 revenue declined by 6% QoQ on seasonality (project deliveries peak in the fourth- quarter). EBIT margin was 3.2%, flat YoY but down from 3.8% in 4Q25, mainly due to heavier QoQ administrative expenses. Operating cashflow s were negative Bt46m, versus positive Bt295m in 1Q25, due to an inventory buildup. As such, the average number of inventory days rose to 4 9, up by five days from 1Q25 and by six days from 4Q25. Outlook We expect SIS’s 2Q26 core profit to decline YoY, as its mobile phone sales operation ( 17% of revenue) is unlikely to repeat the Bt45 -55m in rebate i ncome booked to its 2Q25 financial statements . In QoQ terms, core profit should r ise, supported by gains on inventories on-hand, as sales prices are rising across several product categories. What has changed? 1Q26 core profit comprises 20% of our 2026 forecast of Bt921m (up 1% YoY), in line with 1Q25’s proportion of full-year 2025 earnings of 20%. Recommendation We have shifted down our SIS call from BUY to HOLD, as the remaining upside to our target price is only 4% and we are concerned about the much slimmer GM for IT security products.
